about: How a production-host answer is classed (founder ruling 2026-10-03: "we shouldnt accept vercel.app sites lol, only custom domain sites"; review-2 P3-2/P3-4). vercel: ANY *.vercel.app host (a project's production alias, a team alias, a branch alias, a deployment URL, a nested host), refused: "Infinite needs your site's own domain. <host> is a Vercel address — add a custom domain in Vercel, then run npx infinite-tag again." preview: another platform's default address (*.netlify.app, *.pages.dev, *.github.io) or a local address, refused. bare_platform: a platform domain itself (vercel.app, netlify.app, pages.dev, github.io), refused. custom: not on the deny list, claimable (the site-file proof decides). infinite-tag and the cloud must class every host here the same way.

cases.note: a project's production alias (<project>.vercel.app): refused, the site needs its own domain
case and one trailing dot are normalised away
a deployment URL whose hash has no digit (no shape rule is needed any more)
more than one label under vercel.app
a GitHub Pages default (not the site's own domain; the preview guard's list is unchanged)
a platform domain itself: nobody's site, never provable (review-2 P3-2)
GitHub Pages' platform domain itself (founder ruling 2026-10-03)
a look-alike is not on the deny list
